messages:
anya: Heads-up, running onboarding tests for kepler-64k-int3 and hit a reproducible divergence once context > 131k tokens. Behavior looks like KV lookup returning stale "sentinel" entries around a non-power-of-two boundary.

lee: That number screams 131072 boundary (2^17). Which runtime branch and quant codec?

anya: runtime: release/longctx-optim (with the new rotary clamp). codec: int3-packed v2. Command used: 

```bash
./bin/long_onboard_test \\
  --model kepler-64k-int3 \\
  --context 132000 \\
  --prefill 131200 \\
  --quant int3packedv2 \\
  --kv-map-mode cyclic \\
  --rotary clamp
```

anya: Minimal log: 

```
[2025-09-10T15:04:02Z] prefill=131223
[2025-09-10T15:04:03Z] kv_lookup: token=131071 -> shard=1 local_index=127 (ok)
[2025-09-10T15:04:03Z] kv_lookup: token=131072 -> shard=1 local_index=128 (ok)
[2025-09-10T15:04:03Z] kv_lookup: token=131073 -> shard=1 local_index=-32736  <-- sentinel-ish
[2025-09-10T15:04:04Z] gen: token=131240 fingerprint_mismatch
```

sam: local_index negative big number usually implies an unpack/endianness bug or an uninitialized int16 read. Did you run with ASAN or valgrind?

anya: quick ASAN run attached earlier shows a single memcpy shadow hit inside codec unpacker for packed int3 decode path. But the issue reproduces even with sanitizer off, so it's not just an ASAN artifact.

runtime: We landed a change in the circular kv allocator recently that flips the modulus to use bitmasking when shard size is power-of-two for perf. That optimization might misfire if the logical slot count isn't a clean power-of-two anymore.

lee: try `--kv-map-mode clamp` and `--kv-slot-count 131200` to force non-bitmask path. If the issue disappears it's almost certainly an allocator bitmasking assumption violation.

anya: launching quick variants now: (1) kv-map-mode clamp (2) kv-map-mode cyclic + kv-slot-count 131072 (3) codec int4 fallback.

devops-bot: snapshot uploaded: s3://repro-dumps/kepler/2745554321/trace.tgz (size 42MB)

anya: quick status: clamp -> passes 3/3, cyclic + explicit slot-count(131072) -> mismatch still present, int4 fallback -> mismatch delayed by ~600 tokens but still eventually diverges.

sam: that pattern fits a subtle phase offset introduced by int3packedv2 decode combining with the bitmask index math: when the logical slot count != mask+1, high token numbers can map to incorrect local indexes (garbage). Int4 changes the entropy so mismatch moves but doesn't remove root cause.

lee: request: please `--dump-kv-slots 131000:131250` and `--dump-raw-kv-bytes 131068:131076` and paste the hex. Also rerun with `--no-rotary-clamp` to rule out rotary interplay.

anya: pasted slot dump: 

```
slot 131068: id=131068 header=0x8f3a data_len=64
slot 131069: id=131069 header=0x8f3b data_len=64
slot 131070: id=131070 header=0x8f3c data_len=64
slot 131071: id=131071 header=0x8f3d data_len=64
slot 131072: id=131072 header=0x8f3e data_len=64
slot 131073: id=0 header=0x0000 data_len=0  <-- zeroed sentinel but index mapping points here
slot 131074: id=131074 header=0x8f40 data_len=64
```

anya: raw bytes for 131071..131073: 

```
131071: ff a2 01 7c ... (64 bytes)
131072: ff a2 01 7d ... (64 bytes)
131073: 00 00 00 00 ... (all zeros)
```

lee: confirms: slot 131073 is zeroed but a lookup mapped token -> local_index pointing into it. That matches the local_index=-32736 earlier (bad signed read). Why would mapping target a slot that's zeroed? Either allocator freed it prematurely or map math wrapped incorrectly.

runtime: I'll bisect the recent allocator PRs. Meanwhile, can you try `--kv-preallocate` to force full slot population and `--kv-scan-validate` to verify slot ownership post-prefill? If preallocate fixes it, it's likely a timing window between prefetch and allocation.

anya: `--kv-preallocate` + `--kv-scan-validate` -> passes 5/5. So either allocator race or lazy init. I'll open an urgent runtime PR to disable the bitmask optimization for non-power-of-two logical sizes and add a regression test.

sam: please add a unit test that constructs a non-power-of-two slot count and then prefill crossing that boundary, assert no negative indexes and no zeroed-ownership lookups. Add it under tests/longctx/kepler_boundary_test.py.

anya: filing issue RN: INF-2319, linking trace + dump. Will send PR to runtime with fix + tests and ping this thread. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
